pages.text: Elemental damage is $(l)added on top of$() your ordinary physical hit. It is a bonus, not a replacement, and it is calculated separately.$(br2)With the default settings:$(br2)$(li)Every enchantment level gives $(thing)5 points$()$(li)Every $(thing)10 points$() of Enhancement adds $(thing)0.5 damage$()$(li)So one point is worth $(thing)+0.05 damage$()

pages.title: The calculation
pages.text: In order:$(br2)$(thing)Elemental bonus$() = points / 10 x 0.5$(br2)then multiply by:$(br2)$(li)Restraint (x1.5 or x0.5)$(li)Target Wetness (fire only, -10% per level)$(li)Target Spores (fire only, +10% per stack)$(li)Target Scorched (nature +50%, frost -50%)$(li)Freeze (fire only, x0.5)$(br2)then $(l)subtract$() $(thing)the target's resistance for that element$(): points / 10 x 0.5.

pages.title: Reading the numbers
pages.text: One armour piece caps at $(thing)25 points$() - five levels. Four pieces give up to $(thing)100 points$().$(br2)$(li)25 points = +1.25 elemental damage per hit$(li)100 points = +5 elemental damage per hit$(li)100 resistance = -5 damage from that element$(br2)The flat damage is modest. What you are really buying with points is passing the $(thing)thresholds$() that unlock reactions - most of which want 20 to 50 points.

pages.title: Defence in practice
pages.text: $(li)Resistance only reduces the $(thing)matching element$(); it does nothing against physical damage.$(li)Resistance never blocks a $(thing)restrained$() attacker completely - 10% always gets through.$(li)Damage absorption (golden apples) is eaten by elemental damage $(l)before$() the physical part.$(li)Reaction damage - steam, blasts, auras - uses $(thing)Protection$() and $(thing)Fire Protection$() instead, capped at 25% and 50%.
